parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Nitrosyl chloride, $\text{NOCl}$, can be formed by the reaction between nitrogen monoxide and chlorine, as shown.

$$2\text{NO} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NOCl}$$

The initial rate of this reaction is investigated, starting with different concentrations of $\text{NO}$ and $\text{Cl}_2$. The results obtained are shown in Table 5.1.

Table 5.1

| experiment | $[\text{NO}]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{Cl}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate/$\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{min}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $0.0250$ | $0.0150$ | $3.68 \times 10^{-2}$ |
| 2 | $0.0750$ | $0.0150$ | $3.32 \times 10^{-1}$ |
| 3 | $0.0500$ | $0.0600$ | $5.89 \times 10^{-1}$ |

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Use the data in Table 5.1 to deduce the rate equation for this reaction.

Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use your rate equation from (a)(i) and the data from experiment 1 to calculate the rate constant, $k$, for this reaction. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{NO}_2\text{Cl}$ is another compound containing nitrogen, oxygen and chlorine.

In sunlight, $\text{NO}_2\text{Cl}$ can undergo homolytic fission to release chlorine radicals which can catalyse the conversion of ozone, $\text{O}_3$, into oxygen.

Complete the mechanism for this process.

initiation (homolytic fission) $$\text{NO}_2\text{Cl} \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

propagation step 1 $$\ldots\ldots + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

propagation step 2 $$\ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Ozone reacts with nitrogen dioxide, as shown.

$$\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + \text{O}_2$$

The rate of reaction is first order with respect to $\text{O}_3$ and first order with respect to $\text{NO}_2$.

Suggest equations for a two-step mechanism for this reaction.
